Its single core meaning shows up in many grammatical shapes: translators rendered it as "that" 67 times (33%) and as an emphatic "he" 39 times (19%), with many small combinations like "that he" or "will that" reflecting how it joins surrounding words; in fact 49 of 253 occurrences are absorbed so fully into the phrasing that they get no English word of their own. prose.def: Describing infants who were put outside and abandoned, left exposed to die.
prose.article: ἔκθετος literally means "set outside" and describes babies who were abandoned to die from exposure—a real practice in the ancient world. prose.caution: This word occurs only once in the New Testament, so its range rests almost entirely on outside evidence, and the modern rendering "exploited" differs from the older glosses "cast out" and "exposed."

prose.def: To spread out or stretch forth, as one extends the arms wide or unfurls a sail.
prose.article: This verb means to spread or stretch something out fully — the prefix ἐκ pushes the action as far as it will go, like unfurling a sail. It appears only once in the New Testament, in Romans 10:21, where God spreads out his hands all day toward a disobedient people. In the Septuagint it shows up 6 times across 4 books, every time translating the Hebrew פָּרַשׂ ("to spread out"), and Romans 10:21 itself quotes Isaiah 65:2.
prose.caution: The measured sense label "obstinate" reflects how the surrounding verse is rendered, not this verb itself, which means "stretch out"; with only one New Testament occurrence, confidence is low.
